sun.upright:
Look at the five lads in this card, all swinging staffs, nobody hurt, nobody in charge. An Aries Sun sees that and wants in. Cardinal fire, ruled by Mars, you're built to go first and you like a bit of a contest, so on the surface this is an easy card to be handed. Leo and Aries are trine, four signs apart in the same element, and the card's fire and yours understand each other without any translation. The trouble sits underneath. This card runs on Saturn, and Saturn is in fall in Aries. That's the planet of patience and slow building in the one sign that gives it the least respect, so the part of a contest that needs waiting, planning and doing the boring bit twice is the part you're worst at.

What that feels like is a big appetite and not much stamina for the middle. You'll be first into the argument, first with the idea, first to push back in the meeting, and then it drags on, the other side doesn't fold, and you're bored and looking for a different fight. Two lots of fire make it loud. I've seen Aries Suns win the opening round of every contest they're in and lose half of them a few weeks later, simply because they'd stopped turning up.

At work it can be a rivalry with a colleague that you started for fun and now can't drop. In your body it's the sore knee or the pulled back from training too hard too soon. Choose the one contest that's worth the grind, and let a couple of the smaller ones go unanswered.
sun.reversed:
With the card upside down, an Aries Sun can end up fighting for the sake of it. The argument with your brother about something neither of you cares about. The email you fire back within a minute. The driver who cut you off and got a lecture through the window. Saturn in fall in Aries already means the brake is the weakest part of the machine, and when the card turns over the brake more or less goes.

The rarer version, for you, is the fight you've quietly stopped having because you lost the first round and pride won't let you go back in. Both show up at work, and both show up at home as a short fuse by six o'clock. Go for a hard run or a long swim before the next argument you can feel coming, and see whether it still seems worth having when you get back.

moon.upright:
An Aries Moon deals with a feeling by acting on it. Something stings, you say so or you go for a walk around the block, and that's usually the end of it. The Five of Wands in your tides is five people shoving at once, and your Moon doesn't mind that at all. Leo trines Aries, both fire signs, so there's no clash of temperament. If anything the card feels familiar, a room full of the kind of energy you already run on. What won't sit easily is Saturn. It's the planet the card belongs to, and it's in fall in Aries, which in plain terms means it can't do its job properly here. Saturn is the bit of you that can sit with a hard feeling and wait it out. In an Aries Moon that bit is short-staffed.

So you might feel a restlessness that wants a target. Something's niggling, you don't quite know what, and you catch yourself picking at someone in the kitchen or starting a debate you don't care about, because a scrap is easier than sitting still with it. Same element doubles the heat. On a good day that's lovely, you're lively and brave and quick to forgive. On a tired day it gets prickly, and the people at home feel it first.

Sleep is often where it shows, lying awake with an argument you didn't finish. It shows with a partner too, since the person closest usually gets the spare heat. When the prickle starts, move your body hard for twenty minutes before you open your mouth.
moon.reversed:
Held-in anger is the hard version for an Aries Moon with this card reversed. You decided a fight wasn't worth it, which might even have been sensible, and now the feeling has nowhere to go. It turns into a headache, a clenched jaw, a sharp tone with someone who did nothing. Saturn is weak in Aries, and restraint has never been your strong suit, so when you do try it you tend to overdo it, hold on for three days, and then blow over something tiny.

It usually shows at home, over the dishwasher or whose turn it was to ring the plumber, and in your sleep. Your body carries it as a buzz that won't settle. Say the actual thing that's bothering you to the person it's about, in two sentences, and then go and do something physical.

rising.upright:
Strangers tend to read Aries rising as someone who'll have a go. You come through the door quickly, you're first to speak, and Mars, your chart ruler, gives you a face that looks up for it. Drawing the Five of Wands for your mask adds a scuffle to that first impression. It's a trine, Leo and Aries both fire, so the card doesn't sit awkwardly on you. People just see more of what they'd already see, a person who's quick, competitive and happy to argue. What's missing is Saturn's share. The card runs on Saturn, and Saturn is in fall in your rising sign, so the slower skills, holding back, reading the room, letting someone else go first, are the ones you can't reach easily.

You'll probably notice how quickly new conversations turn into friendly contests. Someone makes a point and you're already making the counterpoint, three sentences in, before you've decided you even disagree. A lot of people like that about you. Some take it as a challenge and come back harder, and then you're sparring with someone you met ten minutes ago. That's fine at a barbecue. With a new boss it can go badly.

In a job interview it helps you look keen and hurts you if the panel wanted a listener. On a first date it can be fun or it can feel like debating club, depending on who's across the table. Let the other person finish two full sentences before you answer anyone new.
rising.reversed:
First impressions tend to go wrong in a particular way when this card turns over on Aries rising. You bristle at a tone that wasn't meant for you, take a harmless question as a challenge, and come across as combative to people who only wanted to say hello. Saturn in fall means the pause you'd need is hard to find, and Mars fills the gap with speed.

It shows in the interview where you ended up arguing with the panel, in the new team that decided early on that you were hard work, and at parties where someone edges away mid-conversation. Occasionally it swings the other way and you hang back at the edge of the room, sulky, because you couldn't find a way in. Walk into the next new situation having decided you don't need to win anything in it, and let the first ten minutes be dull.

sun.upright:
Taurus Suns like to build at their own pace, and they don't enjoy being jostled. Fixed earth, ruled by Venus, you want something good and solid and you're prepared to wait years for it. Then this card turns up, a yard full of people all pushing at once. Leo and Taurus are square, three signs apart and both fixed, and a square between two fixed signs is about as stubborn as friction gets. Neither end wants to move. Fire and earth don't have much natural feeling for each other either, so the card's energy doesn't slide into you. It has to be let in on purpose.

There is one thread you can use. Saturn, the card's planet, rules the last ten degrees of Taurus, the part of your sign that belongs to the Seven of Pentacles, the card of the long wait for a crop. So the effort in this card isn't foreign to you. What the Five asks is that you bring that patience into an actual contest, with other people pushing back, and that's where Taurus gets uncomfortable. You'd prefer to be left alone to get on with it. Once you're pushed, though, you don't give ground, and I've seen Taurus Suns outlast much louder people just by staying where they were.

At work this might be a rival going after the role or the client you'd assumed was yours. With money it can be a negotiation, a pay rise or a price on a house, where you've dug in on a number. Decide which of those you actually care about, and give a little ground first on the other one.
sun.reversed:
When the card is reversed, a Taurus Sun is more likely to refuse the fight altogether. Something needs challenging, the pay that hasn't moved in three years, a colleague taking credit for your work, and you've decided it's easier to put up with it. Venus colours Saturn in your sign, so the patience comes with a pleasant face, and people don't realise how much you're holding until it goes.

That's the other end of it. After a long quiet stretch you can dig in so hard over one small thing that nobody around you understands why. It tends to show at work and around money, and in a friendship where you've gone cool and never said what happened. Pick the one grievance that has actually cost you something and raise it, calmly, before it sets hard.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon settles through the body and through routine. The same chair, the good bread, the walk you always take after dinner, and a house where nobody's shouting. This card is a lot of people shouting. Leo and Taurus are square, both fixed, and fixed signs dig in, so this isn't a mood that blows through by lunchtime. It sits. Fire and earth are neutral elements that need introducing, and here that means the card's restlessness doesn't warm you. It just unsettles things.

From the inside you might notice you're irritable in a slow, heavy way, which is how Taurus Moons get irritable. Someone keeps pushing, at work or at home, and you go still and stubborn and wait for them to stop. Usually they do. Saturn, the planet this card runs on, has a real foothold in your sign, the last decan of Taurus that belongs to the Seven of Pentacles, so you've got more staying power in a standoff than most people. The cost is that you hold the tension in your body while you're outlasting someone. Shoulders, neck, gut. And Venus, your Moon's ruler, would much prefer everyone just got along.

It shows at home when a housemate or partner is in a combative patch and you're soaking it up. It shows in comfort eating after a day of friction, and in sleep that's heavy but doesn't leave you rested. Do one slow, physical thing each evening, cook, garden, run a long bath, and do it without your phone in the room.
moon.reversed:
Stonewalling is the Taurus Moon's move when this card comes up reversed. Something's wrong, you know it, and you've decided to wait it out, so you get quieter and heavier until the other person gives up. Sometimes that works. More often the problem just sits there, and so does the resentment. Saturn has no special dignity in Taurus and takes on your Venus colouring, so it all looks calm and pleasant from outside while the mood underneath goes off like milk.

At home it shows as a silence in a room you share. In the body it can be eating or drinking more than you'd like, or a heaviness that isn't quite tiredness. Tell the person the small thing first, the one that started it, and see whether the big thing still needs saying afterwards.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising doesn't hurry a handshake. Venus rules your chart, and strangers usually meet someone relaxed and solid, the person at the party who's found the best chair and isn't about to give it up. This card has none of that ease. It's quick and scrappy and loud, and drawing it for your mask means the world is meeting you in a more combative mood than you're used to. Leo squares Taurus, two fixed signs at right angles, so when someone pushes, you don't move. The elements don't help either, since fire has no natural bond with your earth, and the card's competitiveness doesn't come naturally to your manner. You have to decide to take it on.

What you'll probably notice is people testing you. The new colleague who contradicts you in your first week. The tradie who tries it on with the quote. The friend of a friend who wants to argue about property prices. Your instinct is to stand there, pleasantly, and let them wear themselves out, and it mostly works, because a Taurus Ascendant can look immovable when it wants to. Saturn has a decan in your sign, the Seven of Pentacles stretch, so there's real patience behind the stillness. What people misread is the stillness itself. Some take it as agreement, and some take it as a dare.

It shows in negotiations, where you're harder to shift than people expect. It shows in a new job, where the quiet can be read as not caring. Next time someone tests you, push back out loud on one small point, so they know the stillness is your choice.
rising.reversed:
Turned over, this card can make Taurus rising come across as immovable in the wrong way. You've decided before the meeting starts, and it shows on your face. People bring you a suggestion and get a pleasant, flat no. Saturn gives the stubbornness stamina and Venus keeps it polite, so nobody quite knows how to argue with you, and after a while they stop trying.

A new workplace might label you difficult before anyone knows you. In dating, calm can look like you're not interested. With neighbours or a landlord, a small dispute can harden into a standoff that lasts a year. Say yes to one small thing you'd normally refuse on reflex, and let people see you change your mind.

sun.upright:
The Five of Wands is basically an argument, and a Gemini Sun rarely minds one of those. Mutable air, ruled by Mercury, you like to be where the talk is fastest, with whatever you're curious about this month on the table, and a room where five people are all making their case is a room you'll enjoy. Leo and Gemini are sextile, two signs apart, an easy angle, and fire and air feed each other. So the card catches quickly. You're sharper, funnier, keener to have a go.

Saturn is what makes this card more than a scuffle, and in Gemini Saturn has no special strength. It borrows your Mercury, which turns its discipline into something about words and follow-through. Can you land the argument? Can you back the clever line with a fact? Can you finish the thing you started three projects ago? That's where the card's effort goes for you. Gemini Suns are brilliant in the opening round and often a bit absent by the third, and I'd guess you already know which of your projects I'm talking about. The Lovers is Gemini's Major, and it's a card about choosing. Here the choice is which of the five contests you're actually in.

At work it can look like being pulled into several debates at once and winning the point in each without anything getting decided. With friends it's arguing for sport, which is fun until somebody's feelings get hurt. Pick one of your arguments and take it all the way to a decision.
sun.reversed:
When the card reverses for a Gemini Sun, the talking takes over from the doing. Six open contests, six clever positions, and none of them going anywhere. You might switch sides in an argument just to see if you can win from the other end, which is fun, and people stop being sure what you think. Mercury colours Saturn in your sign, so the discipline you're dodging is the plain one, saying what you mean and sticking to it.

It shows at work as a reputation for being quick and unreliable, and with friends who've learned not to take your opinions too seriously. A sibling may be the one who says it out loud. Pick one position you actually hold and argue it to the end, even when it gets boring.

moon.upright:
Talking it through is how a Gemini Moon settles. A feeling isn't real to you until you've found the words for it, said them to someone, and heard what they said back. The Five of Wands gives that a crowd. Several voices at once, which honestly isn't far from what goes on in your head on an ordinary Tuesday. Leo sextiles Gemini and fire feeds air, so the card doesn't upset your mood so much as speed it up. You're chattier, quicker, a bit wired.

Saturn is the card's planet, and in Gemini it takes on Mercury's colouring, so the steadying it offers is a mental one. Finishing one thought before the next one grabs you. Staying with a single feeling long enough to know what it is. That's hard for a Gemini Moon, because the mind is always a step ahead of the body, and when you're upset it runs faster. You can end up arguing with yourself, both sides, late at night, and it feels like thinking when really it's worry.

Sleep is the obvious place, lying there rehearsing a conversation you'll probably never have. Messages are another, the long text you draft and redraft, or the group chat that turns snippy over nothing. Before bed, write the worry down in one sentence on paper and leave it on the kitchen bench.
moon.reversed:
A Gemini Moon under this card reversed can't switch the argument off. The same exchange goes round at two in the morning, with better lines each time. Or you talk about everything except the thing that's actually upsetting you, because saying that one out loud would make it real. Saturn in Mercury's colours leans on the thoughts until they start to feel like facts.

You'll notice it in bad sleep, in a jumpy stomach, in chatter that goes on a bit too long at dinner. A friend or a sibling usually picks up on it before you do, and you'll probably tell them you're fine. Ring one person and tell them the plain version in a minute or less, then change the subject on purpose.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising meets people with a question, a joke, and another question. Mercury rules your chart, and people often come away from a first conversation with you feeling they've met three different people, all of them good company. The Five of Wands suits that manner well. It's a card of crossed staffs and crossed talk, and your first impressions already happen at that speed. Leo is sextile Gemini and the elements are friendly, fire lifted by air, so the sparring comes easily and a new room warms up around you fast.

Underneath, Saturn is borrowing your ruler's colours, and what it wants is for your words to carry weight. People enjoy the banter. Then some of them start testing it, quietly, to see if you mean what you say or just like saying it. Gemini rising can pass that test easily if you slow down for a second and give a straight answer. The risk is that you enjoy the fencing so much you never get to the straight answer, and people leave charmed and slightly unsure of you.

It shows in interviews and pitches, where quickness gets you in the door and a clear yes or no gets you the job. It shows on first dates, which can turn into a very entertaining debate about nothing much. In your next first conversation, say one thing you actually believe, plainly, and leave it there.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, the card can make Gemini rising slippery. You deflect with a joke, change the subject when it gets real, win the small exchanges and lose the conversation. Saturn in Mercury's colours is the part of you that would commit to a position, and it's the part that's gone missing, so people come away not knowing where you stand. Now and then it flips, and you argue every point with a stranger to prove you're clever, which lands worse.

It tends to show in a new job, where colleagues can't work out what you think, and in dating, where charm keeps someone at the same distance for months. When someone asks your opinion, give it in one sentence before you make the joke.

sun.upright:
Cancer Suns tend to measure how they're doing by how their people are doing. Cardinal water, ruled by the Moon, you're proud of the home you've made and fierce about who's in it, even when the fierceness doesn't show. The Five of Wands is a hard card to be handed. It's a squabble with no shelter in it, and you feel raised voices in your body. Leo and Cancer sit side by side in the zodiac, neighbours with very little in common, and fire and water are opposed elements, so it's steam, or one putting the other out. Then there's Saturn, the card's planet, which is in detriment in Cancer and working against the grain. The tough, hold-your-ground discipline this card asks for costs you a lot more than it costs most people.

What you'll likely recognise is the way conflict gets into you. A tense meeting at eleven and you're still chewing on it at bedtime. And then there's the side of Cancer people forget. The Chariot is your sign's Major, a driver in armour, and when someone goes after one of your people you'll come out of the shell faster than anyone expected. You don't like a contest for its own sake. You'll win it anyway if it's about family.

At work that can mean a clash with a colleague that spoils your evenings. At home it might be defending a child or a parent in some family argument, harder than you meant to. Before you step into the next fight, ask yourself plainly whose fight it is.
sun.reversed:
With this card upside down, a Cancer Sun tends to take the fight inside and call it hurt. You don't argue. You go quiet, go cool, and keep a careful note of what was said, and the other person might not even know there's a problem. Saturn in detriment in your sign adds a heavy patience to it, and a sulk can run for weeks.

It shows at home, in a household where one person has gone quiet and everyone's walking around it, and in the body, often the stomach. It also shows at work when you do more than your share and resent it silently. Say the hurt out loud while it's still small, to the person it's about, and keep it to what actually happened.

moon.upright:
A Cancer Moon is the Moon in its own sign, so everything is felt at full strength, and what it needs most is somewhere safe to feel it. A home, a person, a routine that holds. The Five of Wands arrives in that like an argument breaking out at the dinner table. This is one of the harder pairings for the card. Leo and Cancer are next-door signs with little in common, and fire against water makes steam, so either the card's heat scalds your feelings or your feelings put it out. Saturn, which the card runs on, is in detriment in Cancer. The bit of you that could stand in the middle of a row and stay steady is working uphill.

From the inside, one sharp exchange can flood you for the rest of the day. You replay it. Something from years ago gets stirred up and joins in, because nothing much ever gets thrown out of a Cancer Moon. And yet there's a fierceness under the softness, and when the conflict is about someone you love, or about your home, you'll hold ground you'd never hold for yourself. That can surprise people, you included.

It shows at home, where the mood in the house becomes your mood within about five minutes. With family, an old sibling rivalry can come back to life over something as small as who's hosting Christmas. When the room heats up, go somewhere quiet and let your body settle before you say anything back.
moon.reversed:
A Cancer Moon with the card reversed is inclined to hold on. The hurt from the argument goes under, gets added to the older ones, and stays. You won't fight, and you won't let go either, and Saturn's discomfort in your sign gives the grudge a heavy, stubborn quality that's hard to shift even when you'd like to.

It shows in moodiness that everyone at home can feel and nobody can name, in a stomach that's off, in sleep broken by the same thought going round. With a parent or a sibling, an old row can come back dressed as a new one. Tell one person you trust what's actually bothering you, while it's still about the argument you just had.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising tests the water before getting in. At a party you'll hover near the kitchen, find the one person who seems kind, and warm up from there, and strangers usually take you as gentle and a bit shy. The Five of Wands asks for a different entrance, straight into the scuffle with your staff up, and that's awkward for you. Leo and Cancer are neighbours with nothing much in common, and the elements pull against each other, fire and water, so a pushy first meeting either overwhelms you or gets quietly damped down. Saturn, the card's planet, is in detriment in your rising sign. Holding a hard, competitive stance at the door is something you can do, and it takes more out of you than it should.

You'll probably notice yourself bracing when someone comes in hot. A loud manager, a stranger with an opinion, a salesperson who won't take no. You go a bit formal, or a bit too nice, and it's all to buy time. The Moon rules your chart, so your face gives it away, and people can often tell you're rattled even when you've said nothing. The good news is that Cancer rising, once it's decided a fight is worth having, is surprisingly hard to move.

In a new job that can mean being read as cold for the first month, when really you're just watching. On a first date, a playful argument might land as criticism. When someone arrives combative, take one slow breath and ask them a question before you answer.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, this card can make Cancer rising shut before anyone's knocked. You're braced for a fight that isn't coming, so a neutral remark lands as an attack and the shell goes up. Or you over-please, agreeing with everyone in the first meeting so there's nothing left to fight about. Saturn in detriment in your rising sign makes the steady, open middle hard to find.

It shows in new groups that decide you're prickly, in a new job where you hear feedback as a verdict, and on dates where you pull back at the first bit of teasing. Your face tends to show the hurt before you've decided whether it's real. Next time someone says something that stings, ask what they meant before you decide.

sun.upright:
This is one of your own cards. The Five of Wands covers the first ten degrees of Leo, ruled by Saturn, so with a Leo Sun you're being handed a piece of your own sign, and it's the awkward piece. Fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, you want to shine and be recognised for it, and you'd like the recognition to arrive fairly naturally. Saturn is in detriment in Leo. It sits opposite its own home here, and everything it does in this sign looks like hard work, because it is. So this is Leo pride that has to earn its place, with other people pushing back and nobody handing over the stage.

Same element doubles everything, the warmth and the wanting to win. From the inside it's the itch to be the best in the room, and the slow, slightly irritating realisation that being noticed and being respected are two separate things, and the second one costs effort. Leo Suns hate looking like they're trying. This card makes you try in public. Strength is Leo's Major, a woman calmly holding a lion's jaw, and that calm is on offer if you stay in the contest long enough. It doesn't come in the first round.

At work you tend to do your best with one real rival to measure yourself against, and your worst when you're competing with everyone at once. In love you want to be chosen, clearly, over the other options. With friends you can turn a dinner into a quiet contest for who's funniest. Pick one arena to be excellent in, and let the others go without keeping score.
sun.reversed:
For a Leo Sun this card reversed goes one of two ways, and both are about pride. Either everything becomes a contest you have to win, the colleague's promotion, the friend's new house, the sibling who's suddenly doing well, or you stop competing altogether and go dim and sulky because nobody's clapping. Saturn in detriment in your sign means the shine always takes some effort, and reversed, the effort starts to show.

At work that looks like taking someone else's success as your loss, and at home in a flatness when there's nobody to perform for. It can show in the body as tiredness from keeping it all up. Find one thing you'd do well even if nobody ever saw it, and do it for a while without mentioning it to anyone.

moon.upright:
The Five of Wands belongs to Leo, and a Leo Moon feels that straight away. Fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, you need to be warm and to be warmly received, to matter to someone and have it shown. This card is your own sign's fire, its first decan, and fire on fire makes every mood bigger. Happier when you're happy. More stung when you're stung. The awkward part is Saturn, which runs this card and is in detriment in Leo. In a Moon, that tends to feel like a nagging sense that love has to be competed for, that you can't simply assume you're wanted.

So you might find yourself keeping track of where you rank. Who replied to whom first. Whether your partner laughed harder at someone else's story. Whether your friends made plans without you. None of it is very dignified and a Leo Moon knows that, which makes it worse. Underneath is a real need, and it's a fair one. You want to be someone's favourite. What gets you into trouble is turning the need into a contest, because then it's about winning, and winning doesn't feel like being loved.

It shows with a partner whose attention has drifted to work or a phone. It shows among friends, where a new person in the group can put your nose out of joint. Say what you want in plain words, something like 'I'd love it if you made a fuss of me on Saturday', and let them do it.
moon.reversed:
A Leo Moon with this card reversed tends to go cold to punish someone for not noticing. You've been overlooked, or you think you have, and you withdraw the warmth and wait to see who comes after it. Saturn's weight on your sign makes it a proud kind of hurt, one that would sooner ache in private than admit it wanted to be chosen.

It shows as a dramatic quiet at home that is very much meant to be noticed, and in a mental list of who called and who didn't. Sleep can go off too, and so can your appetite for the things you usually love. Tell one person, simply, that you felt left out, and let that be the whole conversation.

rising.upright:
Leo rising gets noticed on the way in. The Sun rules your chart, and even on a tired day you tend to arrive as if someone's switched a light on, and people turn round to see who's come in. Drawing the Five of Wands for your mask puts a competitive edge on that. It's Leo's own card, the first decan of your rising sign, so the spark reads as pure you, fire on fire, turned up. The catch is Saturn. It's the card's planet and it's in detriment in Leo, so your first impression is working a little harder than usual. People sense the warmth, and they sense the effort too.

You'll probably catch yourself sizing up who else is holding the room when you walk in. Another big personality, and something in you goes on alert. It's an instinct that can make you sharp and funny and very good company. It also means ordinary gatherings can turn into a quiet contest for the middle of the room, and the people who'd have liked you most might be the quieter ones who never got a word in. I've seen Leo rising do this at weddings and at work drinks alike, and usually not notice.

It shows at networking events and on the first day of a new job, where you're memorable either way. On a first date it can turn into a performance, which is fun for about an hour. Next time you're in a group, ask the quietest person a real question and stay with their answer.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, this card can make Leo rising either blaze or sulk. Some days you dominate every conversation because someone else looked impressive and you felt it. Other days you go flat and aloof, waiting to be approached, which strangers read as arrogance even when it's nerves. Saturn in detriment strips the ease out of your manner, so the warmth comes out brittle. The Sun rules your chart, and it has never much liked sharing a room.

It shows at parties, in the first week of a new job, and on dates where you talk about yourself for too long and know it on the drive home. Let someone else be the most impressive person in the room for an evening, and see how people treat you when you're simply enjoying yourself.

sun.upright:
Virgo Suns want to be properly good at what they do, the kind of good nobody has to check. Mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, you take pride in the job done right, and you notice every corner other people cut. By your standards this card is a mess. Five people waving staffs, no plan, no process, a lot of noise. Leo and Virgo are next-door signs with little in common, so the card's look-at-me competitiveness sits at an odd angle to your heads-down way of working, and fire and earth are neutral, with no natural spark between them. You'll pick up the card's energy only when you decide to.

Saturn has no special dignity in Virgo and borrows Mercury's colouring here, which makes the friction feel familiar in one way. It becomes a contest about being right. You won't be the loudest in the room, and you don't want to be. You want to be the one who read the whole document. That's a real strength, and it can also turn into a quiet competition nobody else knows they're in, where you keep score of other people's mistakes. The Hermit is Virgo's Major, and a lot of Virgo Suns would honestly prefer to stay out of the scrum entirely and be proved right later.

At work it might be a noisy team where you're doing the careful thinking and someone louder is getting the credit. In the body it's tension from holding everything to a standard, jaw, neck, a gut that tightens before meetings. Pick one contest where being right actually changes something, and let the others stay messy.
sun.reversed:
A Virgo Sun with the Five reversed can go to war by correction. You don't fight openly. You point things out, you send the follow-up email with the error highlighted, and people start to feel watched. Mercury colours Saturn in your sign, and reversed, that gives the critique a cold, exact edge. The other way it goes is retreat, fussing over your own corner so you never have to step into the actual contest.

It shows at work in colleagues keeping you at arm's length, and in a body wound tight from standards nobody could meet. Family can get the same treatment, usually over small things. Send out one piece of work that's good enough, and put your hand up for one thing you're not sure you'll win.

moon.upright:
Something useful to do is what a Virgo Moon reaches for when it's upset. You'll reorganise the linen cupboard after a bad phone call, and honestly, it works. This card drops into that as the kind of mess you can't immediately fix, a yard of people squabbling with no system, and your first instinct is to sort everyone out. Leo and Virgo sit side by side and share very little, and fire meeting earth is neutral, so the card's heat doesn't warm you. It just makes more work.

Saturn is the card's planet and takes on Mercury's colouring in your sign, so the pressure lands in your head. You might feel you have to manage the friction perfectly or something will go wrong. A disagreement turns into a checklist of what you should have said. You go over the argument afterwards and find your own mistakes before anyone else's, which is very Virgo Moon and pretty hard on you. There's a small comfort in being the competent one when everyone else is shouting, and you'll probably take it.

It shows in cleaning when the house is tense, in a stomach that reacts to conflict before your head does, and in lying awake editing a conversation that's already over. Do one useful thing to steady yourself, then leave the rest of the mess to the people who made it.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, the Five can turn a Virgo Moon's criticism inward. You replay what you should have said, list your own failings more harshly than you'd ever judge a friend, and Saturn in Mercury's colours gives that inner voice a cold, exacting tone. Or the anxiety leaks out as picking at the people you live with, the wet towel, the way they stack the plates, because the big feeling has nowhere to go.

You'll feel it as over-checking, a tight stomach, broken sleep. Mercury rules your Moon, and when it's anxious it goes looking for something to fix. A partner may notice it before you do. Name the one real thing that's bothering you, kindly and out loud, and let the towel stay on the floor for a night.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising notices things. The stain on the tablecloth, the typo on the name badge, who's nervous and pretending not to be. Mercury rules your chart, and strangers usually pick up that you're paying close attention even when you say very little. The Five of Wands barges in loud and unpolished, which is the opposite of how you like to begin. Leo and Virgo are neighbours with little shared ground, so the brash contest doesn't match your manner, and with fire and earth neutral to each other you'll only step into the fray once you've chosen to.

Saturn takes on your ruler's colouring here, so you meet competition by analysing it. You size up the room, find the flaw in the other side's case, and hold back until you're sure you can do it properly. That's clever, and it means you rarely lose an argument you've picked. Strangers can find it a bit unnerving, though. They feel assessed. I've seen Virgo rising walk into a new team and within a week know exactly who's bluffing, say nothing, and be quietly marked down as aloof for it.

It shows in job interviews, where you'll have the best answers and might forget to smile. It shows in new friendships, where people can't tell whether you like them. Let the first meeting be warm before you start working out what you think of someone.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, Virgo rising can criticise before it connects. You walk into a new situation already looking for what's wrong, the error on the slide, the badly run meeting, and it shows on your face. Colleagues may decide you're hard to please before you've said much. Saturn in Mercury's colours makes the first impression fussy and hard to warm to, and people who might have liked you decide not to bother.

It shows at a first meeting where you came across as unimpressed, and in a new group where your caution looked like disapproval. Occasionally it's the opposite, and you undersell yourself so thoroughly that nobody remembers you were there. Lead with one warm, unplanned thing when you meet someone, and save the assessing for later.

sun.upright:
You'd expect a card of open squabbling to be a Libra Sun's least favourite, and in some ways it is. Cardinal air, ruled by Venus, you care a great deal about fairness and about the people you're partnered with, and you'd usually prefer everyone got along. Look at what drives the Five of Wands, though. It runs on Saturn, and Saturn is exalted in Libra, at its best and most respected in your sign. Saturn is the planet of rules and structure, and in Libra it cares about the fair fight, the contest with proper rules that everyone has agreed to. Leo sextiles Libra, and fire and air are friendly, so the card's energy wakes you up without frightening you.

What you'll recognise is discomfort at the noise and, underneath it, a real talent for refereeing. You can see what each side wants, often more clearly than they can. Saturn also rules the middle decan of Libra, the Three of Swords, the heartache card, and that's the cost you already know about. Fair outcomes still hurt somebody. Libra Suns sometimes put off making the call because of that, and Justice, your sign's Major, holds a sword in one hand for a reason. This card wants you in the contest, making a ruling, and every so often fighting for yourself.

At work you might be the one keeping a competitive team honest. In a relationship you may be quietly weighing who gives more. Among friends you're often the one both sides ring after a falling-out. Make sure one of the sides you weigh fairly is your own.
sun.reversed:
Keeping the peace can become the problem for a Libra Sun when this card is reversed. You smooth things over, refuse to take a side, and let a real imbalance stand because naming it would be awkward. Saturn's exaltation in your sign means you know perfectly well what a fair outcome looks like, which makes it harder, since you're choosing not to ask for it.

It shows in a work rivalry you won't address because you'd like both people to keep liking you, and in a relationship where you've kept a private tally for years and never said a word. Have the fair, slightly awkward conversation you've been putting off, and let it be uncomfortable for as long as it needs to be.

moon.upright:
A Libra Moon needs peace to feel well. You notice the second the temperature in a room changes, and you'll quietly work to bring it back before you let yourself relax. Raised voices get into your body. So a card of five people arguing at once is nobody's idea of a good time for you. There's something on your side, though. Saturn, the card's planet, is exalted in Libra, which means that even in the middle of a row your Moon has an instinct for fairness and a knack for finding the level point. Leo and Libra are sextile and fire and air get on, so the friction doesn't swamp you. It calls on your sense of what's fair.

Still, the need for calm runs deep. A falling-out can throw you for days, even one that isn't about you, and you might find you can't settle until everyone's been heard and things are level again. Libra Moons often weigh the other person's upset against their own so carefully that they lose track of which is which. Venus rules your Moon and wants harmony, and there are times the only road to harmony runs straight through an argument.

It shows in sleep, when there's something unresolved with a friend or a partner. It shows at home, where you'll smooth the room before you can relax in it. Let yourself want a fair outcome for you, even if someone ends up a bit uncomfortable along the way.
moon.reversed:
A Libra Moon with this card reversed swallows its own needs to keep things nice. You agree when you don't, you let someone else choose the restaurant and the holiday and the paint colour, and the buried disagreement turns into a low, aching unease. Saturn, so well placed in your sign, can turn harsh when it's reversed, and you end up judging yourself for every conflict you didn't handle perfectly.

You'll feel it as resentment that has nowhere polite to go, and in sleep that won't come while something between you and someone else is off. The other person may not even know anything's wrong. Say the uncomfortable thing to them, gently, and let things be a bit uneven for a day or two.

rising.upright:
Libra rising puts people at ease. Venus rules your chart, and strangers tend to relax around you within a few minutes without quite knowing why, and they assume you'd like everyone to get on. The Five of Wands looks like a bad fit until you check the astrology. Saturn, which the card runs on, is exalted in Libra, at its most dignified in your rising sign. So you can walk into a room where people are squabbling and start quietly evening it out, and look good doing it. Leo sextiles Libra and fire and air feed each other, so the card's competitive spark comes across in you as charm with some backbone.

You'll probably notice yourself reading the balance of power within a minute of walking in. Who's dominating, who's being talked over, who's about to lose it. You'll adjust without thinking, a question to the quiet one, a light remark to take the heat out. People trust you for it, and they start bringing you their disputes. The thing to watch is that fairness can become a performance, where you're so keen to look even-handed that you never say what you think.

It shows in meetings where you end up chairing without the title, and in negotiations, where your manner makes the other side relax. On first dates it makes you excellent company. Let one strong opinion show early, so people know there's someone definite behind the manners.
rising.reversed:
When the Five is reversed on Libra rising, the charm starts avoiding every hard edge. You agree with everyone at the table, commit to nothing, and tell each person the version they'll like best, which works until they compare notes. Saturn's fine standing in your sign, turned round, leaves you worrying about looking fair when the job was to be fair. Venus hates a scene, so this can go on for a long time before anyone calls it.

It shows in a new group where you charmed everyone and stood for nothing, and at work when you won't take a side in a dispute that badly needs one. On dates it can look like agreeing to things you don't want. In the next meeting, state one clear position and hold it politely.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns don't do casual contests. Fixed water, ruled by Mars and in modern astrology Pluto, you don't do anything halfway, you'd like to hold the keys to your own life, and when you compete, you compete properly. Put the Five of Wands on that and the card's friendly scuffle stops being friendly. Leo squares Scorpio, three signs apart and both fixed, which is about the most stubborn kind of friction there is, and fire and water are opposed elements. The card is showy and out in the open. You prefer to keep your plans where nobody can see them.

Saturn has no special dignity in Scorpio and picks up the colouring of your ruler Mars, so the competition turns strategic. You'd sooner win by knowing more, and you're prepared to wait a long time to do it. From the inside, a rivalry can get under your skin and stay there. You'll think about it on the drive home. You'll remember exactly what the other person said at that meeting last year. That patience is a real weapon, and it can also mean you're still fighting something everyone else forgot years ago. Death is your sign's Major, and part of this card's lesson for you is knowing when a contest is finished.

At work it can be a power struggle that you take personally and plan carefully. In love it may show as a jealous edge when someone seems to be after what's yours. With shared money, you'll guard it closely. Choose which of these deserves your full intensity, because whichever you choose will get all of it.
sun.reversed:
A Scorpio Sun under the reversed Five tends to take the contest underground. There's no open fight. There's a campaign, quiet and patient, run through channels nobody else can see, the email you don't answer, the information you don't share, the person who somehow isn't invited to the next meeting. Saturn in Mars's colouring gives it a cold staying power, and it can run for years.

Work is the usual place, a rivalry that has quietly become a grudge, and so is a relationship where jealousy has gone unspoken and turned into suspicion. Sometimes it ends with you cutting someone off completely. Bring one of these into the open while it's still about the original issue, and say it to their face.

moon.upright:
A Scorpio Moon feels things a long way down and shows very little of it. You need to trust completely or not at all, and you need to feel in charge of your own feelings, which is why open conflict bothers you far more than people realise. This card is conflict out in the open, noisy and public. Leo and Scorpio square each other, both fixed, so this kind of friction doesn't blow over. It settles in. Fire and water are opposed, and here the card's brash heat meets your guarded depths and you get steam, a lot of pressure with nowhere to go.

Saturn, the card's planet, carries the charge of your traditional ruler Mars in this sign, so your feelings around conflict run intense and strategic. Jealousy and suspicion can run much hotter than you'll ever let anyone see. A small slight gets filed away, then turned over, then turned over again. You might not say anything for weeks. You process a wound privately and completely before anyone knows it happened, and by the time you raise it, you've usually made up your mind.

It shows in sleep, when you're replaying a conversation in the dark and deciding what it meant. It shows with a partner, in a loyalty test they didn't know they were sitting. Let one trusted person see the feeling while it's still a feeling, before it hardens into a verdict.
moon.reversed:
A hurt can turn into an obsession for a Scorpio Moon when this card comes up the wrong way round. You circle it, you check, you notice every sign that confirms it, and Saturn in Mars's colouring gives the brooding a grim, unforgiving grip. Sometimes there's a quiet wish for the other person to feel exactly what you felt.

You'll notice it as jealousy you feed in private, as cutting people off at the first hint of disloyalty, and as a body held tight around something you won't say, jaw, shoulders, gut. It can show with family too, in a grudge nobody else remembers starting. Tell someone safe what happened and how it felt, in plain words, and let them see you upset.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising gives off something before you've said a word. People tend to feel sized up, fairly and thoroughly, and a few of them find it uncomfortable. Mars is your chart ruler, with Pluto sharing the job in modern astrology, and even sitting quietly at the end of a table you're the one people keep glancing at. This card is a noisy public scuffle, and when it lands on your first impression it gets pulled down into your quieter register. Leo squares Scorpio, both fixed, so any competition that reaches you turns into a serious matter of who holds the power. Fire against water makes steam, the card's showiness running into your instinct to give nothing away.

Saturn picks up Mars's colouring in your rising sign, so you meet a rival by reading them. You keep your own hand hidden and wait to see theirs. People sense that, and some find it attractive and some find it unsettling. Either way you'll probably be tested, someone pushing to see what's under the guard, and mostly you won't let them. I've seen Scorpio rising win a whole negotiation simply by being the last one to speak.

It shows in business meetings and interviews, where you can seem formidable. In a new friend group, people tend to be intrigued by you and a bit wary for the first few months. Let a new person see one true, unguarded thing early on, and watch what they do with it.
rising.reversed:
Suspicion can arrive before anyone's earned it when this card turns over on Scorpio rising. You read threat into ordinary encounters and keep strangers at a controlled distance, and Saturn in Mars's colouring turns your first impression cold and a little hostile, as if you're braced for a betrayal that hasn't happened. Mars keeps you on guard, and Pluto makes the guard feel necessary.

It shows in coming across as unreadable when you didn't mean to, in treating a new job as a power game, and in shutting someone out at the first ambiguous sign. On a date it can feel like an interrogation, and the other person may not ring again. Give one stranger the benefit of the doubt, on purpose, and see how they handle it.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns like a good argument, as long as it's about something that matters. Mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, you're happiest with something bigger ahead of you, a trip, a cause, a truer answer than the one you had last year. This card, all raised voices and waving sticks, is the kind of scene you'd wander into on purpose. Leo trines Sagittarius, four signs apart in the same element, so the card's fire runs straight into yours and it feels like a game you already know the rules of. Same element amplifies, though, and fire on fire can run away with you.

Saturn has no dignity to speak of in Sagittarius and takes on Jupiter's colouring, and Jupiter likes more of everything. So the card's contest tends to multiply. One cause becomes three, one debate turns into a running campaign. There's a detail on the fact sheet worth knowing too. Saturn rules the last ten degrees of your sign, the stretch that belongs to the Ten of Wands, the man bent double under a bundle of sticks he agreed to carry one at a time. I'd guess you recognise him. Temperance is Sagittarius's Major, and its whole point is mixing things in the right measure, which is the skill this card is asking of you.

At work it's taking on the extra project because the argument for it was so good. With study or travel it can mean turning learning into a competition about who's read more or been further. Among friends it's the political argument you keep reopening at dinner. Drop two of your causes on purpose, and give the one that's left everything you've got.
sun.reversed:
A Sagittarius Sun with the Five reversed can end up fighting on every front at once. Every argument has a principle in it, every principle needs defending, and you're signed up for more battles than one person could ever finish. Jupiter colours Saturn in your sign and inflates the whole thing, and the Ten of Wands decan that Saturn holds in Sagittarius starts to look like your actual calendar.

The other version is a restlessness that bolts the moment something starts to feel like a commitment. It shows at work as overcommitting, in friendships as being righteously right, and in the body as a tiredness you keep outrunning. Write down every cause you're carrying, cross off the ones that aren't really yours, and tell someone you've done it.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room. Space to move, something to look forward to, and a feeling that life is going somewhere good. When a feeling gets heavy, your first move is usually out the door, a walk, a plan, a weekend away. The Five of Wands stirs all that up, and honestly it suits you. Leo and Sagittarius are trine, both fire, so the card's restless heat tends to lift your mood. A bit of friction gives you something to push against, and a Sagittarius Moon often feels most alive in the middle of a lively argument.

Same element does amplify, and the danger is too much. You want stimulation and can't sit still, and when a feeling turns heavy the instinct is to bolt, towards a plan, a trip, a new topic. Saturn takes on Jupiter's colouring in your sign, and the steadying it offers is simple and hard, staying with a feeling that isn't fun. Saturn also rules the last decan of Sagittarius, the Ten of Wands, and that's a fair warning about how restlessness works in you. It says yes to things so it doesn't have to feel something, and then you're carrying all of them.

It shows in booking something when things get tense at home, in debating for sport when you're low, and in a body that needs to roam or it goes flat. When the friction rises, stay in the room ten minutes longer than you want to before you go anywhere.
moon.reversed:
Running from the feeling is the reversed version for a Sagittarius Moon. The next trip, the next idea, the next argument, anything that isn't the heavy thing. Or it flips into preaching, holding onto a belief so hard it's clear your comfort depends on being right about it. Saturn in Jupiter's colours can do either, and both keep the real feeling at arm's length.

You'll notice a restlessness that won't let you rest, and a sharpness with anyone who tries to pin you down, often a partner. Sleep gets patchy, and so does your patience. Friends may notice you've gone either very quiet or suddenly very loud. Sit with one uncomfortable feeling for as long as a cup of tea takes, and don't make any plans while you do it.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising is usually laughing within a minute of arriving. Jupiter rules your chart, and strangers tend to meet someone generous with stories and opinions, honest to the point of bluntness, happy to say the true thing and then laugh about having said it. The Five of Wands over that is an easy fit. Leo trines Sagittarius, fire with fire, so the card's competitive spark reads as your ordinary warmth turned up. You come into a room ready to engage, up for the debate, and people feel the energy straight away. With the fire doubled, though, the bluntness can start more contests than you meant it to.

Saturn runs the card, borrowing Jupiter's colouring in your sign, and there's a detail worth knowing. Saturn rules the last ten degrees of Sagittarius, the Ten of Wands decan, and that's a picture of how your open manner gets you into trouble. You say yes to everyone you meet. You offer to help, to introduce, to come along, and a month later your arms are full. The friendliness is real. The follow-through is where the card's discipline comes in, and strangers do notice which of your offers turned into something.

It shows at parties, where a first conversation becomes a lively argument about politics. It shows at work when you meet a new client and promise more than the timeline allows. Make one offer to someone new and deliver it exactly, on the day you said you would.
rising.reversed:
The frank manner can turn tactless when this card is reversed on Sagittarius rising. You blurt the blunt thing, argue for fun with someone who wasn't having any, and Saturn in Jupiter's colours puffs the first impression up into something preachy or overpromised. Jupiter makes everything bigger, including the gap between what you said and what you did.

It shows in a new group where your honesty landed as rudeness, in a first meeting where you talked big and delivered late, and in a restlessness that won't stay with anyone long enough to be known. On dates it can look like you don't take anything seriously. Say a bit less on first meeting, mean all of it, and let the other person have the last word.

sun.upright:
Saturn is the engine of this card, and Saturn rules Capricorn, so what drives the Five of Wands is your own sign's landlord. A Capricorn Sun is built for the long climb, cardinal earth, ambitious, prepared to do the unglamorous work for years to earn its standing, and the discipline other signs find so heavy in this card is simply how you operate. Saturn is at home in your sign, strong and unforced. What sits oddly is the Leo side of it. Leo and Capricorn are a quincunx, five signs apart with nothing in common, and the card's loud, showy scramble grates against your preference for competing quietly and letting results talk. Fire and earth are neutral too, so the heat has to be taken up deliberately.

From the inside that often looks like a patience other people mistake for not caring. Winning the argument in the meeting doesn't interest you much. Where you'll be in five years does, and you're fairly sure the loud ones won't last. You're usually right. The Devil is Capricorn's Major, though, and it's a card about the chains people put on themselves, and with this card that can be a contest you've stayed in long after it stopped meaning anything, because quitting would feel like losing.

At work it's the long game, where you win by endurance. With money it's building slowly while other people chase quick wins. With family it can be the weight of always being the responsible one in a squabbling household. Keep the discipline, and check once in a while that the top you're climbing towards is one you still want.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun with this card reversed can keep competing out of duty long after the ambition has gone. Saturn is fully at home in your sign, so there's no weakness to blame. The risk is discipline that has set hard, an all-work climb where every rung is just another obligation and nobody, including you, enjoys any of it.

It shows at work in outworking everyone to prove a point you can't quite name, at home in treating play as something you haven't earned yet, and in the body as a tiredness you've decided is normal. Sometimes the fear underneath is simpler, that if you stopped, you wouldn't know who you were. Book something purely for fun, put it in the diary like a meeting, and don't cancel it for work.

moon.upright:
Being useful is how a Capricorn Moon calms down. Hand you a problem and a deadline and your breathing slows, and you'd honestly prefer to be the one people lean on, since leaning on anyone else makes you uneasy. This card meets that like an exam you'd sooner sit alone. There's real strength in the pairing, because Saturn, the card's planet, rules your Moon's sign and is at home there, and a steady, unflappable way of handling conflict is how you're wired. The trouble is Leo. Leo and Capricorn share nothing, a quincunx, and the card's open, emotional showiness sits awkwardly against your reserve and asks for constant small adjustments. Earth and fire have no natural pull on each other, so the heat doesn't stir you. It gets managed.

Under the composure, though, competition can touch an old fear of not being good enough. A lot of Capricorn Moons were the sensible child in the family, the one who noticed the unpaid bill, and it stuck. So when there's friction, you take charge and get on with it, and nobody sees what it costs. You might feel lonely in the middle of a crisis you're running perfectly well. That's a very Capricorn Moon kind of lonely.

It shows in working harder when you're actually hurt, in turning down help you badly need, and in a body that holds stress in the knees, back or jaw. With a parent, the old rivalry over who's the capable one can flare up again. Let one person carry a small part of it with you, and tell them you're glad they did.
moon.reversed:
Locked down is how a Capricorn Moon tends to go under the reversed Five. Conflict comes and you go cold, controlled and entirely self-sufficient. You won't show the hurt, you'll manage it alone, and Saturn at home in your sign gives that self-containment a heavy, joyless discipline.

You'll feel it as burying feelings under work, as a pessimism that expects the worst so it can't be disappointed, and as a body that aches from carrying everything without complaint. A partner may say you've gone distant. Family can feel it too, especially whoever you're usually looking after. Admit to one safe person that you're struggling, in those words, and see what they offer.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising gets handed responsibility early. Saturn rules your chart, and even at twenty you had the look of someone who'd sorted the bills, so strangers still tend to treat you as the adult in the room. Drawing this card for your mask gives you unusual grounding, because Saturn, the planet it runs on, is at home in your rising sign. You meet competition with natural authority, unbothered where other people get rattled, and the card's discipline comes through you as your own. What jars is the Leo flamboyance in it. Leo and Capricorn are a quincunx, so the loud, look-at-me scramble sits at an odd angle to your restraint, and with fire and earth neutral you'll only take it up by choice.

You'll probably notice people treating you as the sensible one before you've proved anything. You'll also catch yourself sizing up the hierarchy in a new room, coolly, and deciding which contest is worth your time. Usually it's the one about competence, and you win it. The five noisy lads in this card would find you slightly intimidating. What you might be short on is warmth. People take you seriously, and some of them find you hard to like at first, and you don't always find out.

It shows in career, in interviews for senior roles, and with anyone official, the bank, the council, a landlord, who tends to trust you on sight. On a first date you'll read as serious and reliable, which suits some people very well. Laugh at something early in your next first meeting, out loud, and let them see it.
rising.reversed:
With the Five reversed, Capricorn rising can harden into a status contest. You're so correct and buttoned up that people feel judged, or you're signalling rank, the title mentioned early, the right name dropped at the right moment, and strangers keep their distance. Saturn at home in your rising sign gives the coolness real staying power, so a first impression like that can stick for months.

It shows at work with people junior to you, who don't know how to approach you, and on dates, where the other person can feel they're being interviewed for a role. Make a small joke at your own expense early in the next new meeting, and leave it there.

sun.upright:
Aquarius and Leo sit opposite each other, and this card lands right on that line. An Aquarius Sun is fixed air, with Saturn as its traditional ruler and Uranus as the modern one, and you're drawn to ideas, principles and the group, and a little suspicious of anyone who needs the spotlight. The Five of Wands is Leo's card, five people each wanting to be the one who's seen. An opposition is the same axis seen from the other end, and it pulls toward balance, so the card is asking you to own some personal ambition you'd usually hand over to the cause.

The link that makes this interesting is Saturn. It's the card's planet, and it's at home in Aquarius, your sign's traditional ruler. The reason Saturn struggles in Leo is that Leo is the sign opposite its home, and its home is you. So this card is Saturn a long way from where it lives, and you're where it lives. That's why the principled, disciplined side of the contest comes easily to you. You'll fight hard about fairness and ideas. What's harder is admitting you'd also like a bit of credit. Fire and air are friendly elements, and the card's heat does feed your air, so you might find you're quite competitive and would prefer people didn't know.

At work it can be competing for a principle while pretending you don't care who gets the credit. Among friends it's standing slightly apart within the group and minding, quietly, when someone else becomes its centre. Let yourself say out loud one thing you want for you, without attaching a cause to it.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with the card reversed tends to go cool and contrary. You argue against things on principle, detach from a contest you're secretly invested in, and stand so far apart from the group that you can tell yourself you aren't competing at all. Saturn, settled at home in Aquarius, can harden this into a rigid kind of aloofness. It can look like confidence from outside. From inside it's usually closer to a fear of being ordinary.

It shows in disagreeing to prove your independence, in friendships held at a careful distance, and at work, where you might wave off a promotion or a bit of praise because wanting it feels beneath you. Tell one person what you'd actually like to win, and let them see you care.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon likes a bit of distance from its own feelings. You'd sooner work out why you're upset than be upset, at least at first, and you can be very clear-eyed about a mood while you're still in it. This card arrives as heat you'll instinctively cool down with analysis. It comes from the sign straight across from your Moon, Leo facing Aquarius, and its hot, personal, look-at-me conflict is exactly the register you tend to step away from. An opposition pulls toward balance, so there's a tug here between feeling the thing and observing it. Fire and air get along, so the friction doesn't drown you. It wakes up the part of you that likes a good argument.

Saturn, the card's planet, is one of your sign's rulers and at home here, so a cool, principled steadiness in conflict is more or less your factory setting. Someone gets upset, and you get calm, and reasonable, and a bit far away. That helps in a crisis. It can also leave the people close to you feeling they're arguing with a very polite wall. Inside, you might notice the odd loneliness of watching your own feelings from the other side of the room, understanding them perfectly and not quite having them.

It shows in explaining a hurt so thoroughly you don't have to feel it, and in needing space the second things get intense with a partner. With friends it's belonging to the group and staying slightly outside it. Next time something stings, say 'that hurt' before you say anything clever about why.
moon.reversed:
An Aquarius Moon under the reversed Five can detach so far it goes numb. You float above a conflict you should be inside, call it being reasonable, and keep everyone at the same cool distance. Saturn at home in your sign gives the aloofness a rigid, self-justifying edge, and you can make a very good case for why you don't need anyone.

You'll feel it as a chilly withdrawal others read as not caring, and a loneliness you won't admit to because needing people feels like weakness. It can show with family, where you've been the calm one so long that nobody asks how you are. Let one person see a feeling that isn't cool or tidy, and stay in the room while they respond.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising comes across as friendly to everyone and close to nobody, at least on first meeting. Saturn and Uranus share your chart rulership, and strangers usually see someone original, a bit detached, clearly their own person. The Five of Wands comes from the sign opposite your Ascendant, and its warm, personal, competitive display is exactly what you usually keep at arm's length. An opposition asks for some balance, so this card is asking you to meet a bit of that heat. Fire and air feed each other, so the contest actually livens your manner up and brings out the part of you that loves a spirited exchange.

Saturn is the card's planet and one of your chart rulers, at home in Aquarius, so you meet rivalry in an even, principled way. You treat everyone as equals in the argument, the intern and the boss alike, and people notice that and like it. Where it gets tricky is that you tend to turn a personal contest into a debate about ideas, and the other person, who was upset about something personal, can feel you've missed the point. Some strangers find you approachable and then can't work out why they don't feel any closer.

It shows in new groups, where you're liked quickly and known slowly. It shows at work in meetings where you argue the principle and someone else takes it personally. Let one new person past the friendly front early, with a real story about yourself.
rising.reversed:
A contrary streak can take over Aquarius rising when this card is reversed. You meet people from behind glass, take the opposite line to prove you're nobody's follower, and keep everyone at exactly the same distance. Saturn at home in your rising sign gives that separateness a rigid, faintly superior set. Strangers can read it as arrogance, which usually it isn't.

You'll see it in a new group where you stood apart so firmly you never actually joined, in disagreeing on reflex in a meeting, and on dates where the debate gets more of your attention than the person does. Join in with something ordinary, a round of drinks, a group photo, and let yourself be one of the crowd for an hour.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns are soft at the edges. Mutable water, ruled by Jupiter and in modern astrology Neptune, you run on imagination and sympathy, and a contest is about the last place you'd go looking for yourself. This card is a lot of egos pushing to win. Leo and Pisces are five signs apart with nothing in common, a quincunx, which means constant small adjustments, and fire and water are opposed elements. The card's aggression either scalds you or gets quietly dissolved, and you'll probably feel a bit of both.

Saturn has no special dignity in Pisces and takes on the colouring of Jupiter and Neptune, which softens its discipline into something dreamier. It's harder to hold a line in your sign. Saturn does have a foothold here, though. It rules the first ten degrees of Pisces, the Eight of Cups, the figure walking away from a row of cups into the night. That's your usual answer to a fight, leaving quietly, and sometimes it's wise. The card is asking whether this is one of those times, or whether you'd be walking away from something that's yours to stand up for. The Moon is Pisces's Major, a card about not seeing clearly, which is how conflict often feels to you.

At work it's absorbing tension that isn't yours and going home drained. In love it can be merging so completely you lose track of your own side of the argument. With friends it's slipping away when things get heated. Hold one small boundary in the next disagreement, and say it in a sentence.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with this card reversed can vanish from the contest altogether. You go vague, drift off, or take on someone else's version of events so you don't have to hold one of your own. Saturn in Neptune's colours can make that look noble, and the Eight of Cups pull in your sign turns walking away into a habit of leaving before anything's settled.

It shows in avoiding a conflict until it festers, in feeling like the victim of a fight you quietly slipped out of, and in numbing the tension with a drink, a screen or a long daydream. Stay for one difficult conversation from start to finish, and say what you think at least once in it.

moon.upright:
Other people's feelings get into a Pisces Moon through the skin. A friend's bad news, a row on the train, a sad film, and you're carrying it home without meaning to, looking for somewhere soft and quiet to put it down. The Five of Wands lands in that like a shout in a quiet house. It's one of the harder pairings for this card. Leo and Pisces share nothing, a quincunx, and fire meeting your water makes steam, so the card's competitive heat either overwhelms your feelings or gets absorbed and drowned in them. Saturn, the planet the card runs on, takes on Jupiter and Neptune's colouring in Pisces, and its discipline keeps slipping through your fingers.

Saturn rules the first decan of Pisces, the Eight of Cups, and in a Moon that shows up as a strong pull to leave. Nothing dramatic. You just go quiet, go to bed early, stop answering, and slip out of the conflict to look for somewhere gentler. From the inside it can be hard to tell whose feelings you're carrying. You come away from a tense lunch exhausted without knowing why, and it takes a day to realise most of what you felt wasn't yours.

It shows in coming home wrung out from a workplace full of big personalities, and in avoiding a confrontation with a family member because it hurts too much to start. The body tends to go foggy and tired under stress. When things heat up, ask yourself which of these feelings is actually yours, and deal with that one first.
moon.reversed:
A Pisces Moon under the reversed card dissolves the conflict into fog and slips away from it. Daydreams, sleep, a haze that keeps the world blurry. You won't fight, you'll disappear, and Saturn in Neptune's colours makes the vanishing feel almost kind, while the Eight of Cups pull has you out the door before anything's faced.

You'll feel it as a low, teary overwhelm you can't trace, and a tiredness that has more to do with avoiding things than with sleep. Someone close may feel they've lost track of you. At work you might agree to everything and then quietly not do some of it. Name one clear feeling to yourself, write it down if that helps, and stay with it until it's had its say.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising arrives softly. Strangers usually meet someone gentle and kind who seems to take on the colour of whatever room they're in. The Five of Wands wants you sharp-elbowed in a scrum, and your instinct at the door is to merge, soothe or quietly slip out the side. Leo and Pisces are a quincunx with nothing in common, so the pushy contest sits at a strange angle to your yielding manner. Fire against your water makes steam, and a combative first encounter either overwhelms you or gets gently absorbed and defused before anyone notices.

Saturn runs the card, taking on Neptune's dreamier colouring in your rising sign, so you meet rivalry by dissolving it. You go vague, deflect with kindness, agree with a bit of everything. Saturn also rules the Eight of Cups decan in Pisces, and that's the part of you heading for the exit while you're still smiling. People like you for it. Then some of them find they have no idea where you stand, and that can come across as slippery, which you'd hate, because it isn't meant that way at all.

In meetings you can be read as agreeing to something you never agreed to. It shows on dates, where you adapt so thoroughly the other person ends up meeting a mirror. Say one thing you disagree with, kindly, in the first half hour of meeting someone.
rising.reversed:
The softness can turn to fog on Pisces rising once this card turns over. At the first sign of friction you blur, deflect, agree without meaning it, and you're present in body and absent in every other way. Saturn in Neptune's colours makes the escape feel gentle, and the Eight of Cups pull has you halfway out the door before anyone notices you've gone.

It shows in a first impression that leaves no clear mark, and in new groups where you merged so completely nobody knows the real you. Occasionally it tips the other way and you overpromise to keep everyone happy. Pick one thing you actually think and say it early, in plain words, so there's an outline for people to meet.

1.upright:
Your body, your face, the way you walk into a room. That's the first house, and it's angular, one of the four corners of the chart, so whatever lands here is visible and gets acted on. With the Five of Wands drawn into it, what's live is a readiness to test yourself. You might notice you're walking into rooms a bit braced, a bit keen for someone to push so you can push back. Aries is the natural sign of this house and Mars its ruler, and Leo trines Aries, fire with fire, so the card feels at home here and turns the heat up.

The catch is Saturn. It's the planet this card runs on, and it's in fall in Aries, the house's own sign. Saturn wants patience, pacing, a plan. The first house wants to go. So you get plenty of fight and not much of the restraint that would aim it, and the energy comes out in odd places, a snappy reply to a shop assistant, a sprint at the end of a run you didn't need. Mercury has its joy in this house, which is why the way you talk and the way you carry yourself are so tangled up here. People read your mood off your face and your first sentence before you've decided what it is.

In the body it's energy that needs a job, or it turns into restlessness and poor sleep. In how you present yourself it can look like a harder edge, a sharper haircut, a firmer handshake. Pick one physical challenge with a start and an end, a race, a course, a hard hike, and point the fight at that.
1.reversed:
The first house with this card reversed tends to stay braced for a contest that isn't coming. With Saturn in fall in this house's sign there's no brake on the reflex, so ordinary days get met as if they were a challenge, the queue, the email, the driver who hesitated at the lights. Or the opposite happens, and you shrink from the one fight that would actually say who you are, and feel oddly flat about it.

It shows in a body wound tight and hard to settle, and in a sense of yourself that has started to lean on having something to push against. Spend the energy on purpose, through exercise and through work that pushes back honestly, and let the small provocations go past.

2.upright:
Your bank balance and your sense of your own value both live in the second house. It's succedent, the kind of house where things get built up and held, and its natural sign is Taurus, ruled by Venus, so it likes things steady and it likes them nice. The Five of Wands brings competition into that. Your income, your savings, what you'd charge for an hour of your time, all start to feel like something you have to win and then defend. Leo squares Taurus, two fixed signs at right angles, and that's real friction. The card's restless fire keeps poking at a house that wants to settle and accumulate.

Fire and earth don't naturally help each other either, so the heat here doesn't grow your money by itself. It stirs it up. Saturn adds a hard, effortful edge, the feeling that anything you have came through a struggle and could go the same way. You might find yourself comparing, the colleague's salary, the friend's renovation, the sibling who bought a place first. That comparing is the card at its least useful.
